segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And he asked him secretly about this matter.
And he revealed to him the blindness of the Caliph,
and that there was a certain woman who wrote these things and imitated the Caliph's handwriting,
and that a eunuch named Rashiq was in league with her,
and that they were writing whatever they pleased without the knowledge of the Caliph.
And from then on, that vizier began to neglect fulfilling the orders that were commanded of him.
And that woman and that eunuch realized that Amin al-Dawla had exposed them,
since he alone of those who could see the vizier and speak with him knew the secret.
Therefore, they suborned two brothers known as the Banu Qamar al-Din,
and they lay in ambush for the physician one night as he left the Caliph's palace and was going home.
And they leaped upon him and stabbed him with two knives.
And when he saw them, he shouted:
"Seize them,
for they are so-and-so and so-and-so!"
And those wicked men heard,
and they turned back again and killed him completely.
And they also struck the one who was carrying a lantern with him;
they struck him with a knife as well.
And at that very moment, the city and the palace of the Caliph were thrown into commotion,
and that deceased man was carried and brought to his house,
and he was buried there.
And after nine months, they carried him to the Church of Mar Thomas,
and buried him with his fathers.
And on the very night that illustrious man was killed,
both of his vile killers were also captured.
And their bellies were ripped open,
and they were impaled in the very place where they had killed the deceased man.
Now that deceased man left three honored sons:
Shams al-Dawla,
Fakhr al-Dawla,
and Taj al-Dawla,
who themselves also attained great honors,
especially the eldest, Shams al-Dawla.
And in this same year,
which is the year 1528 [of the Greeks],
618 of the Arabs, Jalal al-Din Hasan, the head of the Ismailis, died,
and his son Ala al-Din Muhammad succeeded him, being nine years old.
For he had grown up with small boys of his own age in play, rearing sheep, and wandering with camels,
and he surrendered {or: entrusted} the entire administration of his realm to women.
And after five years of his reign,
a certain physician who was among them,
without any illness requiring bloodletting,
opened [a vein]
